rules.title: API Controllers Conventions and Standards
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any new AcmeApp endpoint that is added under v2 instead of v3 by default.
- Flag any new endpoint moved to v4 without being part of the dynamic server-side program-session redesign.
- Flag any endpoint change that adds or keeps functionality in v4 when it is not affected by that redesign.
- Flag any new endpoint added to v2, since v2 is legacy and must not receive new endpoints.
- Flag any endpoint deprecation that does not use the `deprecated_endpoint` helper.
- Flag any deprecated endpoint implementation that is not wrapped in `deprecated_endpoint` before logging starts.
- Flag any deprecated endpoint that is not replaced with a static stub when it is ready to stop serving real data.
- Flag any deprecated endpoint that is not configured to return 404 to all clients via the Flipper flag for its endpoint name.
- Flag any deprecated endpoint that is removed before the 404 phase has been enabled and clients have stopped hitting it.
- Flag any deprecated endpoint whose Flipper slug is changed or not stable across versions.
- Flag any deprecated endpoint that does not pass per-endpoint context via `context: { ... }`.
- Flag any deprecated endpoint context that includes sensitive values such as tokens or passwords.
- Flag any new pagination implementation that does not use an opaque, base64-encoded JSON `pageToken`.
- Flag any pagination implementation that does not treat the token as a black box echoed back as `nextPageToken` / `prevPageToken`.
- Flag any new paginated endpoint that accepts `pageToken` as required instead of optional for the first page.
- Flag any new paginated endpoint that requires `perPage` on every request instead of only on the first request.
- Flag any new paginated endpoint that fails to ignore `perPage` on subsequent requests because it is encoded in the token.
- Flag any new paginated endpoint that does not default `perPage` to 20.
- Flag any new paginated endpoint that does not cap `perPage` at 100.
- Flag any pagination implementation that does not use `DEFAULT_PER_PAGE` and `MAX_PER_PAGE`.
- Flag any pagination implementation that does not encode and decode tokens with `Pagination::PageToken.encode(...)` and `Pagination::PageToken.decode(...)`.
- Flag any pagination token implementation that omits `per_page` from the token payload.
- Flag any pagination token implementation that treats `page` or cursor as required instead of optional.
- Flag any pagination token implementation that does not default to the first page when `page` or cursor is absent.
- Flag any new paginated response that does not include a `meta` object.
- Flag any paginated response whose `meta` object does not contain `nextPageToken`, `prevPageToken`, and `total`.
- Flag any paginated response that does not set `nextPageToken` to `null` when there is no next page.
- Flag any paginated response that does not set `prevPageToken` to `null` when there is no previous page.
- Flag any new endpoint validation error handling that does not return `422` for failed validations.
- Flag any validation error response that does not return an `errors` array.
- Flag any validation error entry that does not include `full_message`, `field`, and `type`.
- Flag any validation error handling that does not use `format_active_record_errors` for model validation errors.
- Flag any validation error handling that does not use `API::AcmeApp::V3::ActiveRecordErrorsFormatter#format_active_record_errors` for model validation errors.
- Flag any validation error handling that hand-rolls the model validation error shape instead of using the existing concern.
- Flag any Grape parameter-validation error handling that does not use `API::AcmeApp::V3::GrapeErrorFormatter`.
- Flag any validation error response that omits nested field paths when needed.
- Flag any validation error response that does not default `field` to `"base"` when no field is applicable.
- Flag any validation error response that translates or otherwise alters the persisted `type` value.
- Flag any validation error response that omits translated `full_message` values.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for a new endpoint path or controller namespace under v2, or a new AcmeApp endpoint not placed under v3 by default.
- In added lines, look for a new v4 endpoint outside the dynamic server-side program-session redesign scope, or a v4 addition unrelated to that move.
- In added lines, look for any new endpoint being introduced under v2.
- In added lines, look for deprecation code that does not call `deprecated_endpoint(...)`.
- In added lines, look for a deprecated action body that is not wrapped inside a `deprecated_endpoint` block.
- In added lines, look for a deprecated endpoint replaced by live logic instead of a static stub.
- In added lines, look for missing Flipper-based 404 behavior for the endpoint slug, or code that still serves the endpoint normally after the 404 phase.
- In added lines, look for removal of the endpoint before the deprecation lifecycle reaches the final removal step.
- In added lines, look for a changed deprecation slug string, or a slug that appears newly invented per release rather than stable.
- In added lines, look for `deprecated_endpoint(..., context: ...)` missing, or context hashes that include tokens, passwords, or similar secrets.
- In added lines, look for pagination params or response code that uses plain page numbers, cursors, or non-opaque tokens instead of base64-encoded JSON `pageToken`.
- In added lines, look for pagination code that does not echo tokens through `nextPageToken` / `prevPageToken`.
- In added lines, look for `pageToken` declared as required on the first request.
- In added lines, look for `perPage` being required on every request, or read from later requests instead of only the first.
- In added lines, look for pagination code that lacks a default of 20 or a maximum of 100, or that hardcodes different limits than `DEFAULT_PER_PAGE` / `MAX_PER_PAGE`.
- In added lines, look for token encode/decode logic not calling `Pagination::PageToken.encode(...)` and `Pagination::PageToken.decode(...)`.
- In added lines, look for token payload construction that omits `per_page`, or makes `page`/cursor mandatory, or fails to fall back to the first page when absent.
- In added lines, look for paginated responses missing a `meta` object or missing any of `nextPageToken`, `prevPageToken`, or `total`.
- In added lines, look for `nextPageToken`/`prevPageToken` being set to something other than `null` when the corresponding page does not exist.
- In added lines, look for validation handling that returns a status other than `422` for failed validations.
- In added lines, look for error responses that do not build an `errors` array.
- In added lines, look for error objects missing `full_message`, `field`, or `type`.
- In added lines, look for model validation error formatting that bypasses `format_active_record_errors` or the `API::AcmeApp::V3::ActiveRecordErrorsFormatter` concern.
- In added lines, look for manually assembled model validation error payloads instead of the shared formatter.
- In added lines, look for Grape parameter-validation error handling that does not use `API::AcmeApp::V3::GrapeErrorFormatter`.
- In added lines, look for validation error payloads that flatten nested field names, omit the default `"base"` field, translate `type`, or omit translated `full_message` values.

rules.title: Domain Organizers Conventions in app/domains
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any new domain organizer module that is not namespaced under the domain noun.
- Flag any new domain organizer module whose name does not match the domain noun.
- Flag any new file path for a domain organizer that is not snake_case and aligned with the constant path.
- Flag any nested concern that is not placed in a subdirectory with matching module nesting.
- Flag any new multi-step logic added outside `app/services/`.
- Flag any new interactor added anywhere.
- Flag any modification that introduces `include Interactor`, `delegate … to: :context`, or `context.fail!` in new code.
- Flag any new value object that is not plain Ruby.
- Flag any new value object that does not define a `.for(record)` constructor.
- Flag any new value object that does not memoize collaborators.
- Flag any new value object that does not expose query methods.
- Flag any user-facing string added without `I18n.t`.
- Flag any swallowed error added without `Sentry.capture_exception`.
- Flag any test file for a domain organizer that is not under `spec/domains/<domain>/…_spec.rb`.
- Flag any test that does not assert the root module delegates to the correct nested class.
- Flag any test that does not use factory_bot for collaborators.
- Flag any test that does not use spy or `have_received` for collaborators.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for new module/class names and file paths whose namespace or basename does not match the domain noun, or whose path is not snake_case / not mirrored by the constant path.
- In added lines, look for nested concern definitions placed directly in a parent file instead of a matching subdirectory and nested module path.
- In added lines, look for new logic classes or methods implementing multi-step workflows outside `app/services/`.
- In added lines, look for `include Interactor`, `delegate` calls targeting `:context`, or `context.fail!`.
- In added lines, look for value object classes that are not plain Ruby objects, or that lack a `.for(...)` constructor, memoized instance variables for collaborators, or query-style methods.
- In added lines, look for string literals or interpolated user-facing text not wrapped in `I18n.t`.
- In added lines, look for rescued/swallowed exceptions without a `Sentry.capture_exception` call before suppressing or returning.
- In added lines, look for spec paths outside `spec/domains/<domain>/..._spec.rb`.
- In added lines, look for specs that omit an expectation that the root module delegates to the intended nested class.
- In added lines, look for collaborator setup that does not use factory_bot, or assertions that do not use spy objects / `have_received`.

rules.title: Interactors conventions and legacy status
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any new interactor being created in `app/interactors/`.
- Flag any multi-step business workflow added to an interactor instead of a service in `app/services/`.
- Flag any interactor code that uses metaprogramming.
- Flag any interactor code that uses concerns or mixins.
- Flag any interactor code that uses raw SQL instead of ActiveRecord when ActiveRecord would fit.
- Flag any business logic placed in ActiveRecord models instead of in an interactor or service.
- Flag any interactor that does not `include Interactor`.
- Flag any interactor that does not define an instance `#call` method.
- Flag any interactor that does not assign outputs onto `context`.
- Flag any interactor that does not signal expected failure with `context.fail!`.
- Flag any code that treats `.call` as returning something other than an `Interactor::Context`.
- Flag any caller of an interactor that does not check `.success?` before using the returned context.
- Flag any caller of an interactor that does not read result data from the returned context attributes.
- Flag any failure handling that uses `raise` for expected domain failures instead of `context.fail!`.
- Flag any failure handling that uses `context.fail!(error: "...")` without attaching caller-readable data to the failed context when needed.
- Flag any attempt to rewrite an existing working interactor into a service solely for consistency or churn reduction.
- Flag any modification to an interactor that is not an existing-behaviour change.
- Flag any interactor spec file not placed under `spec/interactors/<namespace>/<class_name>_spec.rb`.
- Flag any interactor spec that does not stub collaborator services with spy plus `have_received`.
- Flag any interactor spec that does not assert each step ran.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for new files or classes under `app/interactors/` that introduce a new interactor or new multi-step workflow logic.
- In added lines, look for metaprogramming constructs, concern/mixin inclusion, raw SQL strings/queries where ActiveRecord should be used, or business logic added to model classes.
- In added lines, look for missing `include Interactor`, missing `def call`, missing `context.` assignments, or missing `context.fail!` in interactor implementations.
- In added lines, look for `.call` usage followed by direct result assumptions without `.success?`, or attribute reads from something that is not an `Interactor::Context`.
- In added lines, look for `raise` used to represent expected domain failure instead of `context.fail!`, or `context.fail!` calls that do not pass readable failure data when the caller needs it.
- In added lines, look for edits that convert a working interactor into a service without a functional reason, or changes to an interactor that are not modifying existing behaviour.
- In added lines, look for spec paths outside `spec/interactors/<namespace>/<class_name>_spec.rb`, or specs that use plain stubs/mocks instead of spy plus `have_received`, or specs that omit assertions that each collaborator step executed.

examples.snippet:
class CreatePatientTransfer
  include Interactor
  delegate :current_user, :patient, :params, to: :context

  def call
    context.transfer = transfer
    context.fail! unless valid_transfer? && transfer.save
  end
end

# caller
interaction = CreatePatientTransfer.call(current_user: current_user, patient: patient, params: params)
render json: { error: interaction.transfer.errors } unless interaction.success?

# New interactor created for new logic (should be a service instead)
class NewBusinessWorkflow
  include Interactor
  def call; end
end

rules.title: ActionMailer conventions and standards
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any mailer class that does not inherit from `AppMailer` or that subclasses `ActionMailer::Base` directly instead of the app mailer base.
- Flag any domain-specific mailer base that does not extend `AppMailer`.
- Flag any mailer setup that omits the required base behavior provided by `AppMailer`: layout `"email"`, `PreventMailInterceptor`, default sender `noreply_email_from`, `multipart_mail`, or `with_locale`.
- Flag any asynchronous email delivery that is not routed through an `app/tasks/` job and uses `deliver_later`.
- Flag any transactional email that does not use `deliver_now`.
- Flag any mailer action that renders email content without wrapping the subject and body generation in `with_locale(user)` for the recipient.
- Flag any subject that is hardcoded instead of using `t("emails.<domain>.<action>.subject", …)`.
- Flag any subject translation key that does not follow the `emails.<domain>.<action>.subject` pattern.
- Flag any mailer view that is not colocated under `app/views/<mailer>/<action>.{html,text}.erb`.
- Flag any mailer action whose method name does not match the corresponding view filename.
- Flag any mailer that does not use `multipart_mail` when both HTML and text formats are expected to be rendered.
- Flag any attachment assignment that does not use `attachments["program.pdf"] = file.read`.
- Flag any branding or whitelabel logic that does not use `AcmeApp::Branding::App.determine(provider)` for subject prefixes, logos, or app titles.
- Flag any mailer class name that does not follow the `{Domain}Mailer` pattern.
- Flag any namespaced mailer that is not namespaced according to its scope, such as `PatientMailer::MessagesMailer` or `Crm::UserMailer`.
- Flag any mailer spec that is not located under `spec/mailers/…_spec.rb`.
- Flag any mailer spec that does not reuse `shared_examples "a mailer"` from `spec/support/mailer.rb`.
- Flag any mailer spec that does not assert delivery, recipient, and rendering across every available locale via the shared examples.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for mailer classes inheriting from `ActionMailer::Base`, or for missing inheritance from `AppMailer`, or for domain base classes that do not extend `AppMailer`.
- In added lines, look for mailer setup code that lacks `layout "email"`, `PreventMailInterceptor`, `default from: noreply_email_from`, `multipart_mail`, or `with_locale`.
- In added lines, look for `deliver_later` calls outside `app/tasks/` job code, or for async email code that uses another delivery method.
- In added lines, look for transactional email code using `deliver_later` or any delivery method other than `deliver_now`.
- In added lines, look for mailer actions that call `mail` or build the body without a surrounding `with_locale(user)` block.
- In added lines, look for subject strings written literally, or for subject code that does not call `t("emails.<domain>.<action>.subject", …)`.
- In added lines, look for translation keys for subjects that are not under `emails.` or that do not include the domain and action segments.
- In added lines, look for view paths outside `app/views/<mailer>/`, or filenames that do not match the mailer action name, or missing `.html.erb` / `.text.erb` colocations.
- In added lines, look for mailer actions that render only one format when both HTML and text should be produced, or for missing `multipart_mail` usage.
- In added lines, look for attachment code that assigns files in any way other than `attachments["program.pdf"] = file.read`.
- In added lines, look for branding logic that uses custom constants or helpers instead of `AcmeApp::Branding::App.determine(provider)` for prefixes, logos, or titles.
- In added lines, look for mailer class names that do not end with `Mailer`, or for namespaced mailers whose namespace does not match the scoped domain structure.
- In added lines, look for mailer specs placed outside `spec/mailers/`, or for specs that do not include or invoke `shared_examples "a mailer"` from `spec/support/mailer.rb`.
- In added lines, look for mailer specs that omit assertions for delivery, recipient, or rendering across all locales.

rules.title: ActiveRecord Model Conventions
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any model code that contains business logic instead of persistence-related concerns.
- Flag any model code that adds callbacks for external side effects such as emails, jobs, or API calls.
- Flag any model code that uses callbacks when they are not necessary for maintaining denormalized data or sanitizing input.
- Flag any model query logic that uses raw SQL instead of ActiveRecord query methods.
- Flag any AR-unfriendly query logic that is kept in a model instead of being moved to a named query object in `app/scopes/`.
- Flag any query that interpolates user input directly into SQL.
- Flag any model file whose path does not match its constant path under Zeitwerk naming conventions.
- Flag any use of `ignored_columns` that remains after the column has been removed.
- Flag any newly added Single Table Inheritance hierarchy in a model.
- Flag any model test that is not placed in `spec/models/<model>_spec.rb`.
- Flag any model spec that tests business behavior instead of validations, associations, scopes, or persistence-related callbacks.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for non-persistence logic in models, especially service-like branching, orchestration, or domain behavior outside validations/associations/basic data management.
- In added lines, look for `before_save`, `after_commit`, or similar callbacks that trigger emails, enqueue jobs, call APIs, or otherwise cause external side effects.
- In added lines, look for callbacks added without a clear persistence-maintenance purpose such as denormalization or input sanitization.
- In added lines, look for raw SQL fragments in model queries, such as SQL strings used where ActiveRecord scopes, `where`, `joins`, or `merge` should be used.
- In added lines, look for complex query objects or query methods defined in the model that should instead live as a named query object under `app/scopes/`.
- In added lines, look for SQL strings built with string interpolation or concatenation from user-controlled values instead of bind variables or hash conditions.
- In added lines, look for file paths and constant/module names that do not align with Zeitwerk mapping between `app/models/...` and the declared constant path.
- In added lines, look for `ignored_columns` declarations that are being introduced or retained after the corresponding column is already gone.
- In added lines, look for new `inheritance_column`/STI-style subclassing patterns or new model hierarchies that imply Single Table Inheritance.
- In added lines, look for spec files placed outside `spec/models/<model>_spec.rb` for model-level tests.
- In added lines, look for specs asserting business workflows or service behavior inside model specs instead of validations, associations, scopes, or persistence-related callbacks.

examples.snippet: where("foo = #{val}")
where("foo = ?", val)
after_commit :send_welcome_email # External side effect in callback

# In app/services/user_signup.rb
user.save!
Mailer.send_welcome_email(user)

rules.title: Policy Objects Conventions
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any policy object in `app/policies/` that is not a plain PORO with no base class.
- Flag any policy constructor that does not take domain objects as inputs.
- Flag any public policy method that is not a predicate-style question about the domain.
- Flag any policy that is being used as an authorization framework instead of a business-rule predicate object.
- Flag any policy code that introduces or relies on a Pundit `Scope` class.
- Flag any policy code that assumes a policy-lookup mechanism exists.
- Flag any policy that does not surface reasons with `ActiveModel::Errors` when the caller needs the reason.
- Flag any policy that uses only a boolean return where the rule requires an error/message reason.
- Flag any policy that omits optional `.allowed?` or `.for` class factories when used for one-line call sites.
- Flag any policy rule that is feature-flagged but does not use `Flipper.enabled?(:flag, user)`.
- Flag any policy message that is not produced with `I18n.t`.
- Flag any policy class name that does not follow `{Concept}Policy`.
- Flag any policy class that is not namespaced by domain when the domain requires it.
- Flag any policy spec outside `spec/policies/…_spec.rb`.
- Flag any policy spec that does not instantiate the policy directly.
- Flag any policy spec that does not assert predicates with matcher-style expectations.
- Flag any policy spec that uses Pundit matchers.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- Added lines define a policy class under `app/policies/` with inheritance from a framework base class, or with a non-PORO superclass/module pattern.
- Added lines show an initializer that takes controller, request, current_user, or other framework objects instead of domain objects.
- Added lines define public methods that perform authorization checks, controller permission logic, or non-predicate behavior rather than answering a domain question.
- Added lines reference Pundit concepts such as `Scope`, `policy_scope`, or policy lookup/dispatch behavior.
- Added lines add comments, methods, or usage implying this policy is part of CanCanCan/Pundit authorization instead of a business-rule object.
- Added lines return only `true`/`false` where the surrounding code indicates the caller needs an explanation, or they omit `ActiveModel::Errors` usage entirely.
- Added lines add a class factory or call-site helper pattern but omit `.allowed?` or `.for` where a one-line factory is expected.
- Added lines gate behavior with a feature flag using anything other than `Flipper.enabled?(:flag, user)`.
- Added lines build user-facing messages without `I18n.t`.
- Added lines declare a policy class name that does not end in `Policy`, or that is missing the domain namespace required by the rule.
- Added lines create or modify specs outside `spec/policies/…_spec.rb`.
- Added lines in policy specs instantiate via framework helpers instead of `described_class.new(...)` or equivalent direct construction.
- Added lines in policy specs assert with Pundit matchers or authorization matchers instead of predicate expectations like `expect(policy).to be_...`.

examples.snippet:
class RepeatableProtocolPolicy
  def initialize(protocol)
    @protocol = protocol
  end

  def repeatable?
    return false unless protocol&.provider && Billing::Status.for(protocol.provider).practitioner_access?

    protocol.repeat_week? && active? && protocol.total_weeks < Rails.application.config.max_program_weeks
  end
end

class RepeatableProtocolPolicy < ApplicationPolicy
  class Scope
    # ...
  end
end

rules.title: Serializer Patterns and Conventions
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any new serializer that is not a plain Ruby object (PORO) unless it is being added inside the existing `api/v3/` serializer area that already uses `jsonapi-serializer`.
- Flag any new `ActiveModel::Serializer` subclass or serializer built on the `attributes` DSL.
- Flag any serializer change that does not match the pattern already used in the area being edited.
- Flag any new serializer outside `api/v3/` that uses `jsonapi-serializer` / `include JSONAPI::Serializer`.
- Flag any new PORO serializer that does not take the record and optional `scope` in `initialize` and expose `as_json`.
- Flag any aggregate/props PORO that does not use a `.call` class method returning a frozen Hash.
- Flag any serializer naming that does not use `{Concept}Serializer` for serializers.
- Flag any audience/version namespacing that does not match the constant path convention.
- Flag any props/aggregate PORO name that keeps the `Serializer` suffix instead of using a suffix like `Props` or `Data`.
- Flag any file path that does not mirror the serializer constant path.
- Flag any date formatting in serializers that does not use `I18n.l` or explicit time-zone conversion.
- Flag serializer specs that do not assert the output hash shape and custom logic.
- Flag serializer specs that test the framework instead of the serialized output behavior.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for `class ... < ActiveModel::Serializer`, `attributes ...`, or other AMS-specific serializer definitions.
- In added lines, look for a new serializer class outside `api/v3/` that includes `JSONAPI::Serializer` or inherits from `API::V3::BaseSerializer`.
- In added lines, look for serializer code that is not a plain Ruby class/object with `initialize(record, scope = ...)` and an `as_json` method.
- In added lines, look for aggregate/props objects that define instance serialization instead of a `.call` class method, or that return a mutable Hash rather than a frozen one.
- In added lines, look for class names or filenames that omit `Serializer` for serializers, or use names that do not align with the constant namespace/path.
- In added lines, look for date/time formatting done with raw `strftime`, manual string building, or other formatting that is not `I18n.l` or explicit time-zone conversion.
- In added lines of specs, look for expectations on framework internals, serializer class type, or DSL behavior instead of assertions on the resulting hash keys/values and custom logic such as nil handling, key casing, or date formatting.

examples.snippet:
class NewSerializer < ActiveModel::Serializer
  attributes :id, :title
end

rules.title: Service Object Conventions in app/services/
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any service object in `app/services/` that is not a plain Ruby class with a `.call` class-method entry point using keyword arguments and delegating to an instance `call`.
- Flag any service object in `app/services/` that inherits from `ApplicationService` or mixes in a module/concern.
- Flag any service object in `app/services/` that uses metaprogramming for dispatch or method definition.
- Flag any service object in `app/services/` that includes concerns or other mixins instead of using object composition.
- Flag any service object in `app/services/` whose methods are not private by default, or that exposes public instance methods other than `.call`.
- Flag any service object in `app/services/` that uses raw SQL inline instead of ActiveRecord, or embeds an AR-unfriendly query directly instead of isolating it in `app/scopes/` or `app/services/queries/`.
- Flag any business logic placed in `app/models/` instead of `app/services/`.
- Flag any user-facing string produced by a service that is not routed through `t()`.
- Flag any service class name or namespace that does not follow domain-noun namespacing and verb-first action naming.
- Flag any service result object that does not use nested `Success`/`Failure` structs with `.success?`, or that relies on a shared base class or gem.
- Flag any service result shape that does not use `errors:` for controller-facing localized string arrays or `error:`/`error_code:` for service-to-service symbol codes, or that branches on `result.error.is_a?(...)` instead of a symbol code when distinguishing failures is required.
- Flag any service that raises for expected business failures instead of reserving `raise` for genuinely unexpected conditions.
- Flag any SQL fragment that interpolates dynamic values or column names into a SQL string instead of passing them through `sanitize_sql_array` or `Arel.sql` with bind variables.
- Flag any supporting non-service PORO in a service namespace that is forced into a `.call` service shape when it should instead fit its own purpose.
- Flag any non-service PORO in a service namespace whose naming does not match its role: noun-first when reused across calls, verb-first when invoked once like a function.
- Flag any service spec not located at `spec/services/<namespace>/<class_name>_spec.rb`, or that does not follow the required testing style (`factory_bot`, spy + `have_received`, no `let`).

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for service classes under `app/services/` that lack `def self.call(...)`, use positional args, or instantiate nothing before delegating to an instance `call`.
- In added lines, look for `class ... < ApplicationService`, `include ...`, `extend ...`, or `ActiveSupport::Concern` in service objects.
- In added lines, look for `define_method`, `send(` with dynamically built method names, string interpolation inside method dispatch, or other runtime-generated method names.
- In added lines, look for `include`/`extend` of helper modules in service objects where a collaborator class could be passed instead.
- In added lines, look for public instance methods besides `call`, or explicit `public` declarations making other methods public.
- In added lines, look for `connection.execute`, raw SQL strings, inline `SELECT ... OVER (...)`, or query logic embedded in the service instead of a separate query object path under `app/scopes/` or `app/services/queries/`.
- In added lines, look for domain logic methods added to models (`app/models/`) rather than services.
- In added lines, look for hard-coded user-facing text in services instead of `t(...)`.
- In added lines, look for class/module names that are not domain-noun namespaces with verb-first service classes, or non-service POROs whose names do not match noun-first/verb-first guidance.
- In added lines, look for `Success = Struct.new`, `Failure = Struct.new`, `.success?`, `errors:`, `error:`, `error_code:`, or a shared result base class/gem pattern that violates the required result shape.
- In added lines, look for `raise` used in normal failure paths, or branching on `result.error.is_a?` rather than symbol codes.
- In added lines, look for SQL string interpolation (`#{...}`) in SQL fragments, dynamic `ORDER BY`/column names inserted directly, or missing `sanitize_sql_array`/`Arel.sql` bind usage for dynamic fragments.
- In added lines, look for supporting objects in service namespaces that are written as `.call` services despite being concept objects/transformers/rule objects, or whose names do not match their invocation/reuse pattern.
- In added lines, look for spec files outside `spec/services/<namespace>/<class_name>_spec.rb`, or specs using `let`, missing factory_bot, or not using spies with `have_received` for collaborators.

examples.snippet:
class Patients::Invite < ApplicationService
  def call
    # ...
  end
end

rules.title: ERB View Templates: Keep Dumb, Use React for New UI, and Follow Tag/Convention Standards
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any new ERB view added under `app/views/` for a new UI or feature instead of implementing that UI in React under `client/`.
- Flag any change that extends `app/assets/javascripts/`.
- Flag any ERB in `app/views/` that contains business or presentation logic beyond formatting/composition, including more than a one-line conditional.
- Flag any ERB change that should be moved to a helper, presenter, or view object because the template is holding logic.
- Flag any use of `raw`, `html_safe`, or `sanitize` on user-provided content that is not clearly reviewed for XSS safety.
- Flag any user-facing string hardcoded in ERB instead of using `t()`.
- Flag any element intended for Capybara feature specs that uses `data-testid` instead of `data-test-id`.
- Flag any reusable UI rendered inline in ERB instead of via a partial.
- Flag any layout section content that is not implemented with `content_for` and `yield` where appropriate.
- Flag any standalone view spec added for ERB views.
- Flag any ERB tag used contrary to its convention: `<% ... %>` for output, `<%= ... %>` without output, `<%# ... %>` for non-comments, or `<%- ... -%>` without whitespace control need.
- Flag any default escaped output changed to unescaped output without a clear sanitization review.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for new `.erb` files or ERB content under `app/views/` that introduce a new screen/feature instead of React code under `client/`.
- In added lines, look for modifications under `app/assets/javascripts/`.
- In added lines, look for conditionals, branching, data shaping, iteration, or other non-formatting/composition logic in ERB, especially conditionals longer than one line.
- In added lines, look for complex inline Ruby in templates that should be extracted to `app/helpers/`, a presenter, or a view object.
- In added lines, look for `raw`, `html_safe`, or `sanitize` applied to values that can come from users, without an explicit XSS-safe review signal.
- In added lines, look for literal user-visible text in ERB instead of `t(...)`.
- In added lines, look for `data-testid=` on elements meant for feature-spec selectors.
- In added lines, look for repeated markup or component-like blocks rendered directly instead of `render partial: ...`.
- In added lines, look for layout-specific content inserted without `content_for` / `yield` structure.
- In added lines, look for new `spec/views/` files or standalone view-spec patterns.
- In added lines, look for ERB tag misuse: output tags used for non-output, non-output tags used for output, comment tags used as code, or whitespace-control tags used without a clear need.
- In added lines, look for `html_safe`/`raw`-style changes that remove escaping from previously escaped output.

examples.snippet: <%= render partial: "shared/user_card", locals: { user: @user } %>

<% if current_user.admin? && @post.published? && @post.author_id == current_user.id %>
  <%= @post.title %>
<% end %>

rules.title: Zustand Store and Bundle Management Rules
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any added code in a bundle that uses a generic `useStore` instead of that bundle’s named Zustand hook.
- Flag any added store hook that does not match the bundle-specific hook name convention for `pt/`, `direct_app/`, or `shared/`, or that introduces a hook name inconsistent with the bundle’s own naming.
- Flag any added slice that is not created under `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/storeSlices/<sliceName>.{ts,js}`.
- Flag any added slice that is not exported from `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/storeSlices/index.{ts,js}`.
- Flag any added slice that is not wired into `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/store.{ts,js}`.
- Flag any added store consumption that subscribes to the whole store instead of destructuring only the needed selectors.
- Flag any added nested state update that does not use `immer` via `set(produce(draft => ...))`.
- Flag any added deep-clone or hand-rolled nested update logic used instead of `immer`.
- Flag any added slice that appears to exceed roughly 200 lines and is not split into smaller slices.
- Flag any added Redux-backed class component change that does not introduce a functional wrapper reading from the Zustand store.
- Flag any added Redux-backed class component change that does not pass Zustand state down as props from the wrapper.
- Flag any added Redux-backed class component change that does not move toward converting the class component to a function component and removing the wrapper when appropriate.
- Flag any added Redux slice or Redux-backed state addition, since new Redux slices are not allowed.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- Look for added imports, hook calls, or variable names showing `useStore` being used in a bundle instead of the bundle’s named hook.
- Look for added hook definitions/usages whose names do not match the bundle-specific store hook expected for `pt/`, `direct_app/`, or `shared/`.
- Look for added files outside `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/storeSlices/<sliceName>.{ts,js}` when a new slice is being introduced.
- Look for added slice code without a corresponding export in `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/storeSlices/index.{ts,js}`.
- Look for added slice code that is not referenced or composed in `client/app/bundles/<bundle>/store.{ts,js}`.
- Look for added store reads that pull the entire store object or otherwise avoid selector destructuring.
- Look for added state mutation code that updates nested fields without `set(produce(draft => ...))`.
- Look for added cloning patterns or manual object/array spreading intended to copy deeply nested state.
- Look for added slice files with large contiguous additions or file content suggesting a slice over about 200 lines without being split.
- Look for added wrapper components around class components that are missing a Zustand store read in the wrapper.
- Look for added class component integrations where Zustand-derived data is not passed through props.
- Look for added class component migrations that stop at the wrapper and do not show a path toward converting the class to a function component and removing the wrapper.
- Look for any added Redux slice definitions, Redux store wiring, or Redux-backed state additions in the diff.

examples.snippet: const state = useAcmeStore(); // Subscribing to the whole store is prohibited

rules.title: I18n Locale Management and Translation Standards
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any newly added user-facing string literal in Ruby, ERB, or React that is not resolved through i18n.
- Flag any newly added controller/view/component string literal that a translator would need to localize.
- Flag any newly added translation key or locale file path that does not live under `config/locales/`.
- Flag any newly added locale file naming/layout that does not follow the existing structure, or that invents a new layout instead of using `en.yml`, `<feature>.en.yml`, or a mirroring directory tree.
- Flag any newly added translation reference in views/controllers that does not use lazy lookup (`t(".foo")`) where appropriate.
- Flag any newly added shared string reference that does not use an explicit dotted key path.
- Flag any newly added translation key path that is deeply nested at 4 or more levels when a shallower path would be possible.
- Flag any newly added translation key that is added to code without also being added to the relevant `*.en.yml`.
- Flag any newly added translation key that is added to `*.en.yml` without a corresponding reference from calling code.
- Flag any newly added translation work that omits automatic translation for `pl`, `es`, `ja`, `ko`, `fi`, and `ro`.
- Flag any newly added locale entries for other languages that are manually added instead of left missing for the translator workflow.
- Flag any newly added translation key that appears not to have been normalized with `i18n-tasks normalize`.
- Flag any newly added translation that changes product names Acme, AcmeApp, or AcmeAssistant.
- Flag any newly added translation that alters text enclosed in `< >` characters.
- Flag any newly added translation that changes interpolation placeholders, removes them, or places them incorrectly.
- Flag any newly added translation that makes a verb or adjective agree with a `%{variable}` placeholder.
- Flag any newly added translation that puts a placeholder in a declined form instead of keeping it nominative or restructuring around it.
- Flag any newly added translation that is overly literal where a more natural, idiomatic rendering is needed.
- Flag any newly added Finnish translation that uses `potilas` instead of `asiakas`, `ohjelman luoja` instead of `ohjelmaeditori`, or `tiheys` instead of `frekvenssi`.
- Flag any newly added validation message override that is not placed in locale files under `activerecord:` or `activemodel:`.
- Flag any newly added email template string that is not placed in locale files.
- Flag any newly added email layout content that is not placed in `app/views/mailers/`.
- Flag any newly added route or URL slug that is routed through i18n instead of remaining English.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added Ruby/ERB/React lines, look for quoted string literals shown directly to users instead of `t(...)` or the frontend i18n equivalent.
- In added controller/view/component lines, look for any literal text that a translator would need to localize.
- In added locale-related lines, look for paths outside `config/locales/` or new locale files placed elsewhere.
- In added locale filenames/paths, look for names or directory structures that do not match the existing pattern and introduce a new layout.
- In added view/controller translation calls, look for missing lazy lookup syntax where the key should resolve from the current path.
- In added shared-string translation calls, look for keys that are not fully dotted and explicit.
- In added locale keys, look for nesting that reaches 4 or more levels deep.
- In added code and locale diffs together, look for a key referenced in code but absent from the relevant `*.en.yml`, or present in `*.en.yml` without any new code reference.
- In added translation-related lines, look for missing locale entries for `pl`, `es`, `ja`, `ko`, `fi`, and `ro`, or for manually added extra locales.
- In added locale-file changes, look for keys that appear unnormalized or oddly formatted relative to `i18n-tasks normalize`.
- In added translation text, look for altered product names, any edits inside `< >`, changed `%{variable}` placeholders, or placeholder placement that breaks grammar.
- In added translated sentences, look for verbs/adjectives that visibly agree with a placeholder, or for placeholders that appear declined instead of nominative.
- In added translation text, look for stiff/literal phrasing where the sentence could be restructured more naturally.
- In added Finnish text, look for `potilas`, `ohjelman luoja`, or `tiheys`.
- In added locale overrides, look for `activerecord:` / `activemodel:` entries placed outside locale files.
- In added mailer-related text, look for strings outside locale files or layout content outside `app/views/mailers/`.
- In added route/slug lines, look for i18n lookup usage for URLs instead of plain English slugs.

examples.snippet: flash[:notice] = "Profile updated successfully"

# config/locales/en.yml
# en:
#   profiles:
#     update:
#       notice: "Profile updated successfully"

# app/controllers/profiles_controller.rb
flash[:notice] = t(".notice")

rules.title: Database Migration Safety, Performance, and Style Standards
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any migration that adds an index on a large table without `algorithm: :concurrently`.
- Flag any migration that adds an index on a large table without `disable_ddl_transaction!` at the top of the migration.
- Flag any migration that adds `NOT NULL` to an existing column in a single step instead of using two migrations.
- Flag any migration that uses `change_column_null` to enforce `NOT NULL` on a large existing table.
- Flag any change that is only a data backfill and is implemented as a migration instead of a MaintenanceTask.
- Flag any `add_column` with a default when the default is a function expression.
- Flag any foreign key added without `validate: false`.
- Flag any foreign key validation done in the same migration as the foreign key addition.
- Flag any rename on a hot table.
- Flag any column rename or drop without checking and updating dependent DB views in a staged migration.
- Flag any migration that changes indexes or rewrites queries for performance without before-and-after `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` measurements in the PR description.
- Flag any performance migration whose measurements are not taken on a representative dataset.
- Flag any migration that bundles more than one logical change.
- Flag any reversible migration that uses `up`/`down` instead of `change`.
- Flag any irreversible migration that uses `change` instead of `up`/`down`.
- Flag any migration filename that is manually timestamped instead of being generated by Rails.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added lines, look for `add_index` on a large table and check whether `algorithm: :concurrently` is present; if not, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for a migration class adding an index and verify `disable_ddl_transaction!` appears at the top; if absent, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for an existing-column `NOT NULL` change done directly with `change_column_null` or a single-step constraint addition; if so, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for a data-only backfill implemented inside a migration rather than a MaintenanceTask under `app/tasks/maintenance/`; if so, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for `add_column` with a default value that is a function call or expression; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for `add_foreign_key` without `validate: false`; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for foreign key validation performed immediately in the same migration as the foreign key creation; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for rename operations on hot tables; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for column rename/drop operations without corresponding staged view updates; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for performance-related index/query migrations without any indication that before-and-after `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` results are captured in the PR description; if absent, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for performance migration notes that reference non-representative data such as tiny dev datasets instead of production replica or seeded staging data; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for a migration that combines multiple logical schema changes in one file; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for a reversible migration defined with `up`/`down` rather than `change`; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for an irreversible migration defined with `change` rather than `up`/`down`; if present, it violates the rule.
- In added lines, look for manually chosen timestamp prefixes in migration filenames instead of generator-assigned timestamps; if present, it violates the rule.

examples.snippet: add_index :patients, :email

disable_ddl_transaction!

def change
  add_index :patients, :email, algorithm: :concurrently
end

rules.title: Search Infrastructure Conventions (lib/search/)
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any change that assumes the Typesense search config is global instead of environment-scoped.
- Flag any change that modifies the hybrid-search distance threshold without an explicit A/B plan.
- Flag any use of `ClientWrapper.upsert` that relies on field merging instead of full-document replacement.
- Flag any split-write design where multiple background jobs write different subsets of the same document unless the jobs are disjoint, serialized through one indexer, or the write is a true full-document upsert from a single source of truth.
- Flag any search-related test that uses mocks instead of a real Typesense container.
- Flag any unit or integration coverage that does not test the integration boundary against real Typesense when that boundary is involved.
- Flag any new Algolia-backed index or new Algolia-backed search path.
- Flag any new search index that does not define its collection schema under `lib/search/typesense/schemas/`.
- Flag any new search index that does not register a sync job emitting via `ClientWrapper.upsert` or batched `import`.
- Flag any new search index that lacks an integration spec against the real Typesense container.
- Flag any new hybrid/vector search index that does not confirm both the embedding model and the distance threshold.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- Look for added code that treats a Typesense config value as shared across all environments, or removes/ignores an env gate around the hybrid-search config.
- Look for added code that changes the search distance threshold constant/config value in `lib/search` without accompanying A/B-plan-related changes or justification.
- Look for added code that calls `ClientWrapper.upsert` while constructing only a partial document or otherwise depending on merge behavior.
- Look for added code that introduces multiple jobs writing to the same document ID with different field subsets, without serialization, disjoint document ownership, or a single-source full-document upsert path.
- Look for added test code that stubs/mocks Typesense instead of using the real `typesense` container.
- Look for added specs that only spy on `ClientWrapper` without any real-container integration coverage for the boundary being tested.
- Look for added Algolia index definitions, Algolia-backed sync/search code, or new references that expand Algolia usage.
- Look for added schema files or schema registration code for a new index that are not placed under `lib/search/typesense/schemas/`.
- Look for added index/job wiring that does not emit through `ClientWrapper.upsert` or batched `import`.
- Look for added search index code without a real-container integration spec.
- Look for added hybrid/vector search code that omits explicit embedding-model selection or distance-threshold confirmation.

rules.title: RSpec Testing Standards for Backend
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag specs that use `let` or `let!` instead of inline setup in each `it`.
- Flag specs that rely on large `before` blocks for setup.
- Flag specs that use `create` when persistence is not needed and `build` or `build_stubbed` would suffice.
- Flag specs that verify collaborator interactions without using spy + `have_received`.
- Flag specs with multiple assertions when they do not all describe the same behavior, or that otherwise violate the one-assertion-per-test guideline when practical.
- Flag specs that compare serialized responses or hashes with partial matchers or fragment checks instead of exact whole-payload equality.
- Flag specs that assert whole payloads without freezing time and using literal timestamps in the expected hash.
- Flag specs whose `it` names describe the method called rather than the expected behavior.
- Flag specs that assert private mechanics, framework behavior, or framework memoization/options instead of observable behavior and the class’s own decisions.
- Flag specs that use unrealistic fixtures, omit fields the real client sends, use incorrect embedding dimensions, or fail to assert mutations additively.
- Flag specs that cover only the happy path and omit edge cases or error branches.
- Flag specs that would still pass if the code under test were reverted, or that assert values that could arise without the code under test.
- Flag specs that create records with loops or helper logic instead of explicit literal factory calls.
- Flag unit specs that test more than one class or fail to isolate the class from its collaborators.
- Flag unit specs that do not stub app classes/services/jobs the class calls and do not assert interactions with spy + `have_received`.
- Flag unit specs that stub datastore behavior instead of keeping the datastore real, or that add fake gems.
- Flag unit specs that stub anything other than genuine external boundaries such as AWS Bedrock, payment gateways, or third-party HTTP.
- Flag unit specs that test framework behavior or private-method mechanics instead of the class’s own decisions and branches.
- Flag unit specs that are not fast and deterministic, including specs that use network, unfrozen time, or unseeded randomness.
- Flag controller specs instead of request specs for HTTP API coverage.
- Flag specs that mock Redis or Typesense instead of using the real services provided by docker-compose.
- Flag specs that add `mock_redis` or stub `Typesense::Client`.
- Flag specs that depend on live `Time.now`, `Time.zone.now`, or `Date.today` instead of freezing time.
- Flag specs that let randomness drive pass/fail, including assertions on random values.
- Flag specs that use `SecureRandom` for anything other than uniqueness.

rules.title: Prefer Database Constraints Over Application-Level Locking
rules.rule: When database constraints such as exclusion constraints or unique indexes can enforce data integrity, avoid using application-level locks or broad transactions. Rely on database-level errors (e.g., PG::ExclusionViolation) to handle conflicts safely and only wrap operations in transactions when cross-record consistency is truly required.

examples.snippet:
MonitoringEpisode.transaction do
  MonitoringEpisode.lock.where(provider: provider, starts_at: range).exists?
  MonitoringEpisode.create!(provider: provider, starts_at: starts_at, ends_at: ends_at)
end

begin
  MonitoringEpisode.create!(provider: provider, starts_at: starts_at, ends_at: ends_at)
rescue PG::ExclusionViolation
  # overlapping episode is silently dropped
end

rules.rule: When rendering UI components that depend on filtered or conditional data, add guards to handle cases where the selected item is absent from the available options. This prevents crashes when the underlying data set does not include the expected value.

rules.rule: Never build SQL fragments by interpolating user input directly into strings, even inside quoted values. Use parameterized queries or ActiveRecord methods so that malicious input cannot break out of the intended clause.

rules.title: Account for Soft Delete Semantics
rules.rule: When a model uses soft deletion, ensure downstream logic treats deleted records appropriately. Do not perform hard-deletion side effects, such as purging associated data, on records that are only being marked as deleted.

rules.title: Controllers: orchestration-only HTTP entry points conventions
rules.rule:
WHAT TO VALIDATE:
- Flag any controller action that passes raw `params` directly to a model or other persistence call instead of using a private `*_params` method.
- Flag any controller action that lacks a private `*_params` method for each action that accepts input.
- Flag any controller code that contains business logic beyond simple CRUD-and-render orchestration.
- Flag any controller action that implements search, filter, or pagination logic inline when an existing service/abstraction should be extended instead.
- Flag any raw SQL in controller code.
- Flag any controller code that persists or renders user input without sanitizing it first.
- Flag any flash message, error response, or redirect copy in controller code that is hard-coded instead of using `t()`.
- Flag any authorization logic in controllers that uses hand-rolled role checks instead of `authorize! :action, resource`.
- Flag any controller action that does not call `authorize! :action, resource` early when authorization is required.
- Flag any plain controller added for a browser surface that is placed outside the approved plain-controller locations.
- Flag any Grape endpoint added for a JSON API or token/OAuth API that is placed outside the approved Grape locations.
- Flag any new endpoint that uses the wrong framework for its consumer type.
- Flag any Grape API code that renders inline JSON hashes instead of using serializers.
- Flag any Grape param declarations that are not in snake_case.
- Flag any API change that removes an existing field without being additive and contract-updated in the same change.
- Flag any new endpoint spec that is written as `type: :controller` or placed outside `spec/requests/`.
- Flag any unit spec for Grape helpers/action classes that is not mirrored to the app path.

HOW TO VALIDATE:
- In added controller lines, look for direct model calls or persistence calls receiving `params`/`params[...]` instead of a private `*_params` helper, or for missing `def ..._params` methods alongside new input-handling actions.
- In added controller lines, look for nontrivial branching, calculations, query construction, or multi-step domain decisions that are not simple orchestration, or for actions that grow beyond a few lines without delegating to a service/interactor.
- In added controller lines, look for inline search/filter/pagination code, especially loops, scopes, or query-building logic, instead of delegation to an existing service/abstraction.
- In added controller lines, look for SQL fragments such as `find_by_sql`, `where("...")`, `joins("...")`, `order("...")`, or other raw SQL strings.
- In added controller lines, look for rendering or persistence of user-supplied values without `sanitize`, `strip_tags`, or parameterized query usage.
- In added controller lines, look for literal flash/error/redirect strings instead of `t(...)`.
- In added controller lines, look for role/permission conditionals like `if current_user...`, `unless admin?`, or similar hand-rolled checks instead of `authorize!`.
- In added controller lines, look for actions that perform protected work before any `authorize! :action, resource` call.
- In added route/controller path lines, look for new plain-controller endpoints outside `app/controllers/pt/`, `app/controllers/physi_app/`, `app/controllers/pt/jane_sdk/`, or `app/controllers/api/iframe/` for browser surfaces.
- In added route/controller path lines, look for new Grape endpoints outside `app/controllers/api/physi_app/`, `app/controllers/api/v3/`, `app/controllers/api/{pms_api,companies,import}/`, or `app/api/` for API consumers.
- In added framework/route lines, look for a framework choice that conflicts with the consumer type described by the endpoint.
- In added Grape response lines, look for `render json:` with inline hashes instead of serializer usage.
- In added Grape param DSL lines, look for `requires`/`optional` keys written in camelCase or otherwise not snake_case.
- In added API diff lines, look for removed fields, replaced fields, or other non-additive contract changes without corresponding staging verification and doc updates in `doc/physiapp-api/`.
- In added spec lines, look for `type: :controller` or new endpoint specs outside `spec/requests/`.
- In added unit spec lines for Grape helpers/action classes, look for paths that do not mirror the app path.
